static_traits.name: Li Jie
static_traits.family_status: Lives with husband (husband was formerly a salesman)
static_traits.social_status: Having a few friends, but unwilling to discuss one's guilt and anxiety with them
static_traits.medical_history: No similar problems occurred before; no psychotherapy history; no notable physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Expresses clearly, positive attitude, able to describe guilt and anxiety concretely; others not mentioned

basic_info.main_problem: A few months ago I accidentally interrupted a call between my husband and a potential client, causing him to lose a deal and break his perfect sales record. I feel intense guilt and anxiety, and whenever my husband is on a sales call or in a client meeting I repeatedly worry I will cause harm again.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because feelings of guilt and anxiety have begun to affect my daily life and put pressure on my relationship with my husband.
growth_experiences: A few months ago, the client accidentally interrupted a phone call between their husband and a potential client, causing the husband to lose an order and breaking his previous perfect sales record. The stress was great when the incident happened; afterward the client's anxiety worsened, and worry and self-blame would arise whenever the husband made sales calls or met with clients; the client tried to make up for it by supporting and helping the husband even more, but the guilt persisted, affecting daily routines and sleep.

Since childhood, influenced by the parents, the client has long participated in church and choir activities; religion and church are important family traditions and faith connections. In recent months, because of busy work at the music store, the client has been unable to attend church on time; on Sundays and when thinking of the absences, the client feels strong guilt and self-deprecation, worrying about disappointing the parents and God, and therefore tends to bear it alone rather than express it to the parents.

core_beliefs: I must perform perfectly and cannot make mistakes

special_situations.event: A few months ago, accidentally interrupted the phone call between the husband and a potential client, causing him to lose the order and breaking the perfect sales record
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my behavior causes my husband's work to suffer, it means I am a bad person and unforgivable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Doubling support and help for the husband to make up for a fault
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I ruined his perfect record; it is all my fault

special_situations.event: Whenever the husband makes sales calls or meets with clients
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: As long as I am not careful enough or not present, I may cause negative effects again, so any disturbance must be avoided
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Highly vigilant and overly careful while the husband works, staying as far away as possible to avoid disturbing him
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This time my mistake may again affect his work

special_situations.event: On Sundays, or thinking about not having attended church recently
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not go to church, it means I am a bad person and will disappoint my parents and God
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids discussing this matter with the parents, blames the self inwardly, and tries to forcibly schedule time to conform to the norm
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I have disappointed my parents and God

special_situations.event: When talking with friends involves topics of guilt and anxiety
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I express my true feelings, they will not understand and may even look down on me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding in-depth discussion of one's feelings with friends

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized by parents and husband, to be accepted as a 'good person', and to maintain a harmonious and secure intimate relationship
core_conflict.fear: Fears disappointing significant others, being judged as a bad person, and triggering relationship estrangement or rupture
defense_goal: Avoiding disappointing others through doubled compensation and self-blame
Reducing direct communication to avoid triggering negative evaluations and conflict

object_relations.self_representation: A guilty 'bad child', someone who constantly needs to make up for faults
object_relations.object_representation: Parents are strict judges, authorities who are easily disappointed
The husband is someone easily disappointed, influenced by oneself

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor asks whether they are willing to communicate with the parents about the guilt and struggle over not attending church
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client worries the parents will be disappointed and look down on them (transference: regarding the parents as harsh judges)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Use a gentle, empathic tone; acknowledge their worry, invite them to provide concrete evidence; jointly explore low-risk, step-by-step communication methods; avoid blame and use open-ended questions.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking about whether to share real feelings of guilt and anxiety with friends
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client believes friends will not understand or will look down on them (transference: projection)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Maintain an accepting and non-judgmental tone; validate the rationality of their experience; gently inquire about past concrete experiences and evidence; encourage trying to express feelings in small steps and observing feedback.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When focusing on the husband's sales calls and the topic of the 'perfect record', and the client shows intense self-accusation
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client attributes all responsibility to themselves and believes that only perfect performance can be accepted (transference: regarding important others as conditional acceptors)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Labels their self-criticism in a non-judgmental, steady tone; guides responsibility redistribution and reality testing; uses gentle rhetorical questions to help them identify supporting and refuting evidence.

manifestations: Unwilling to express true feelings and guilt to parents and friends
Bearing guilt and anxiety alone, believing others will not understand
Feels conflict and constraint between the 'should' demands of religious and family values and real work responsibilities
Difficulty arranging faith and life at one's own pace
outcomes: Limited autonomy, difficulty balancing life and faith

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Frequently uses the self-demand 'I should go to church'
Directly internalizing parental and religious norms as standards for self-judgment

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'. Language manifestations include: 'He is looking down on me', 'They want to exclude me', and so on
manifestations: Believing friends 'do not understand my guilt'
Worrying that parents will be 'disappointed and look down on me'

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'. Language manifestations include: 'It is all my fault that he was hurt', 'I do not deserve to talk to him', and so on
manifestations: Excessive self-blame, believing oneself has 'ruined husband's perfect record'
Being hypervigilant while husband works, deliberately avoiding any possible disturbance

positive_force: Willing to seek counseling and has a positive attitude
Able to engage in reality testing and propose more balanced ideas (such as maintaining a faith connection during the week)
Committed to work, strong sense of responsibility
Tries to repair the relationship by supporting and helping the husband
negative_force: Cognitive distortions such as catastrophizing, personalization, mind reading and 'should' statements
Excessive self-blame and self-denial, relying on external evaluation to confirm self-worth
Avoiding direct communication with parents and friends, insufficient use of social support
Persistent worry leads to disrupted sleep and daily rhythm
Viewing others' reactions as judgment of self-worth, rigid internal standards

target_behavior.behavior: Excessive anxiety and self-blame occurring while husband is engaged in sales activities
target_behavior.core_reason: Personalizing attribution and catastrophically predicting the worst outcome, believing they must be perfect or else they will harm the husband's work and the relationship
target_behavior.function: Escapes potential mistakes and uncertainty through excessive vigilance and avoiding disturbances, gaining a brief sense of control
target_behavior.consequence: Relationship with the husband is tense, daily life and sleep are affected, with persistent worry and guilt

target_behavior.behavior: Strong guilt and self-deprecation about not attending church
antecedent: 周日或想到not yet参加教堂
target_behavior.core_reason: Introjected religious and family 'should' standards, and mind-reading the disappointment of parents and God, lead to strict self-judgment
target_behavior.function: Maintains a feeling of moral consistency through self-blame and avoids direct conflict with the parents
target_behavior.consequence: Low mood, decreased self-worth, disturbed sleep, and avoidance of communicating with the parents
